'''John Francis Burke''' (July 22, 1922 – November 2, 2011) was an American [[medical researcher]] at [[Harvard University]] widely known for his co-invention of [[synthetic skin]] in 1981, together with Dr. [[Ioannis V. Yannas]].
<ref name="NYT">{{Cite news |last=Vitello |first=Paul |date=2011-11-05 |title=Dr. John F. Burke, Dies at 89; Created Synthetic Skin |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/11/06/us/dr-john-f-burke-dies-at-89-created-synthetic-skin.html}}</ref>
<ref name="TEL">{{Cite web |date=2011-11-07 |title=John Burke |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/8875241/John-Burke.html |access-date=2024-04-05 |website=The Telegraph |language=en}}</ref>
<ref name="LAT">{{Cite web |last=Siegel |first=Marc |date=2011-11-14 |title=The Unreal World: 'The Skin I Live In' |url=https://www.latimes.com/health/la-xpm-2011-nov-14-la-he-unreal-world-skin-20111114-story.html |access-date=2024-04-05 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref>
<ref name="NYT2">{{Cite news |date=1976-01-05 |title=Artificial Skin Being Tested for Victims of Burns |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1976/01/05/archives/artificial-skin-being-tested-for-victims-of-burns-animaltissue.html?sq=%2522Dr.%2520John%2520F.%2520Burke%2522&scp=3&st=cse |work=New York Times |pages=40}}</ref>
<ref name="NYT3">{{Cite news |last=Altman |first=Lawrence K. |date=1981-04-24 |title=ARTIFICIAL SKIN FOR BURN VICTIMS IS REPORTED DEVELOPED IN BOSTON |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/04/24/us/artificial-skin-for-burn-victims-is-reported-developed-in-boston.html |work=New York Times |pages=A1}}</ref>
Burke was also widely noted for developing a system of infection control in hospitals and showing that antibiotics given before surgery lower risks of post-operative infections.<ref name="NYT"/> Burke was head of the Shriners Burns Institute and chief of trauma services at [[Massachusetts General Hospital]],<ref name="TEL"/> a professor of surgery at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="TEL"/>

== Life ==
Burke was born in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]] on July 22, 1922.<ref name=":2">Ancestry.com. ''Cook County, Illinois, U.S., Birth Certificates Index, 1871-1922''[database on-line]. Provo, UT, USA: Ancestry.com Operations, Inc., 2011.

Original data:

"Illinois, Cook County Birth Certificates, 1878–1922." Index. FamilySearch, Salt Lake City, Utah, 2009. Illinois. Cook County Birth Certificates, 1878–1922. Illinois Department of Public Health. Division of Vital Records, Springfield.

"Illinois. Cook County Birth Registers, 1871–1915." Index. FamilySearch, Salt Lake City, Utah. Illinois. Cook County Birth Registers, 1871–1915. Illinois Department of Public Health. Division of Vital Records, Springfield.</ref> His father, Francis A. Burke, was a railroad man; his mother was Mary Biaggi.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=John Francis Burke |url=https://fa.hms.harvard.edu/sites/g/files/omnuum4521/files/hmsofa/files/memorialminute_burke_john_f.pdf |access-date=6 April 2026 |website=[[Harvard University]]}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

In 1952, he married Agnes Redfearn Goldman. They had four children, three sons and a daughter.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Burke attended the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] and received a degree in chemical engineering in 1947.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-04-04 |title=NIHF Inductee John Francis Burke Revolutionized Artificial Skin History |url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/john-francis-burke |access-date=2024-04-05 |website=www.invent.org |language=en}}</ref> He received his medical degree from [[Harvard Medical School]] in 1951.<ref name="NYT" /> He enlisted the day after [[Pearl Harbor]] and became an Army Air Corps pilot.<ref name=":0" /> He flew  [[North American P-51 Mustang|P-51]] and [[Lockheed P-38 Lightning|P-38]] fighters.<ref name=":1" /> After World War II, he worked at [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] and Harvard Medical School.<ref name=":1" />

Burke studied the use of antibiotics in the [[Perioperative|perioperative period]] to reduce the risk of bacterial infection.<ref name=":0" />

He participated in a number of major advances in burn care.<ref name=":0" /> Burke performed experimental and clinical work at Shriners Burns Institute (now known as Shriners Hospital for Children – Boston).<ref name=":0" />

=== Appointments ===
Source:<ref name=":0" />

* President of the American Burn Association (1981-1982)
* Board of Directors of the American Trauma Society (1982-1988)
* President of the Surgical Infection Society (1983-1984)
* President of the Boston Surgical Society (1984-1985)
* Chairman of the General Clinical Research Center Committee of the National Institute of Health (1987-1988)
* Governor the American College of Surgeons (1988-1992)
* President of the New England Surgical Society (1989-1990)

== Death ==
Burke died on November 2, 2011 in [[Lexington, Massachusetts]].<ref name="NYT" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-11-07 |title=Pioneering burns surgeon John Burke, a creator of synthetic skin, has died {{!}} Harvard Magazine |url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/node/33987 |access-date=2024-04-05 |website=Harvard Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards ==

* Cutty Sark Science Award (1982)<ref name=":0" />
* Founders Award of the Society of Biomaterials (1982)<ref name=":0" />
* Nathan Smith Distinguished Service Award from the New England Surgical Society (1984)<ref name=":0" />
* Joseph Sussman Memorial Award (1987)<ref name=":0" />
* Distinguished Alumni Award of the University of Illinois (1991)<ref name=":0" />
* Harvey Stuart Allen Distinguished Service Award from the American Burns Association (1993)<ref name=":0" />
* Tanner Vandeput-Boswick Burn Prize in Paris (1994)<ref name=":0" />
* Whittaker International Burn Prize in Italy (1996)<ref name=":0" />
* Jacobson Innovation Award of the American College of Surgeons (1999)<ref name=":0" />
* Distinguished Service Award from the American Association of Tissue Banks (2000)<ref name=":0" />
* Prize of the International Society of Surgery/Societe Internationale de Chirurgie (2003)<ref name=":0" />
* Honorary Award from the American Association of Plastic Surgeons (2008)<ref name=":0" />
* [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]] (2015)<ref name=":1" />
